candidates.title: HiNa-MoE: High-Performance, Non-Intrusive MoE Inference on CPUs with Matrix Engines
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference is increasingly deployed in local and on-premise environments, where expert parameters often exceed GPU memory capacity. In latency-sensitive, low-concurrency settings, repeatedly staging routed-expert weights from CPU memory to the GPU can be prohibitive, leaving routed-expert feed-forward networks (FFNs) on the critical path of multi-socket CPUs. Existing CPU accelerations often rely on intrusive, hardware- or topology-specific requirements, such as AMX-specific weight layouts or manual NUMA-aware placement. These requirements reduce portability and complicate integration with standard CPU-GPU offloading pipelines. We present HiNa-MoE, a high-performance, non-intrusive operator library for MoE inference on CPUs with Intel AMX. HiNa-MoE (1) exploits AMX with an optimized micro-kernel that keeps expert weights in standard layouts and instead fuses lightweight layout transforms into token gathering and stores; (2) applies NUMA-aware task partitioning under a simple page-interleaved policy without modifying the framework allocator; and (3) converts decode-phase memory matrix-vector operations into small matrix-matrix execution to utilize AMX. Across multiple MoE models, HiNa-MoE achieves up to 3.37x speedup for FFN kernels and up to 2.09x end-to-end inference speedup over state-of-the-art baselines, while remaining plug-and-play with existing frameworks and deployment workflows.
candidates.reason: CPU上のMoE expert FFNをIntel AMXで高速化するが、frameworkの重みlayoutやNUMA allocatorに侵襲的変更を要求しない演算ライブラリ。gather/store内で軽量layout変換を融合し、page interleave前提のNUMAタスク分割とdecodeの小行列化でAMXを利用する。著者要旨は既存方式比FFN kernel最大3.37倍、end-to-end推論最大2.09倍を報告。CPUオフロード時のMoE推論演算最適化としてaccept。

candidates.title: APEX: Speculate smarter, not deeper
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding reduces large language model inference latency by drafting multiple tokens before target-model verification, but its effectiveness depends on both the proposal mechanism and draft depth. Fixed configurations cannot respond to changes in predictability, repetition, and acceptance during generation, so deeper drafting can increase wasted computation without proportional speedup. We introduce APEX, a learned controller that balances decoding speed and draft-token waste through request-level expert selection and block-level depth adaptation. APEX-Router selects among EAGLE-3, n-gram, and draft-model speculation for each request, while APEX-Depth adjusts draft length at each verification block using causal decoding signals and recent verifier feedback. APEX models accepted draft length as censored survival feedback, learning position-wise rejection hazards, block execution costs, and an action utility that balances throughput, accepted progress, and wasted tokens. This allows the controller to adapt speculation while retaining the target model's verification procedure. We integrate APEX into vLLM and evaluate it with Qwen3-8B across six workloads, achieving up to 5.24X speedup over autoregressive decoding. Across the aggregate evaluation, APEX-S achieves 4.27X speedup, while APEX-B achieves 3.27X speedup with a 41.0% relative reduction in wasted-token percentage compared with fixed n-gram speculation at k=16, providing distinct operating points for balancing acceleration and draft-token utilization.
candidates.reason: 投機復号のdraft方式とdraft長を固定せず、requestごとにEAGLE-3、n-gram、独立draftモデルを選び、検証blockごとに受理履歴・推論費用を使ってdepthを調整する。受理長を打ち切り観測として学習し、位置別棄却hazardと無駄token費用を推定する。vLLM/Qwen3-8Bで著者要旨は通常AR比最大5.24倍、集計APEX-S 4.27倍、APEX-B 3.27倍と報告。runtimeの動的投機制御としてaccept。

candidates.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute
candidates.abstract: A large language model can only use the text that fits in its context window, and it recomputes its internal key-value (KV) state for a prompt every time the prompt is sent. We test a memory layer, the public package galahad-kv, that saves the KV state of each block of about 16,000 tokens to encrypted local NVMe disk and loads it back later, byte-exact, without recomputing it. We ran it on 50,000,000 tokens of real public text, served through vLLM on one NVIDIA H100, with Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 31B. Every block we probed was loaded back from the encrypted store with no recompute (100 of 100, at depths from 0 to 50M tokens) on both models. Loading a block was 2.8x to 4.3x faster than recomputing it and used 8.8x to 12.3x less GPU energy, and GPU memory stayed flat over the whole 50M-token stream. Asked about facts planted millions of tokens earlier, the 12B model gave the right answer 82 times out of 100 and the 31B model 98 times out of 100. Neither model made up an answer. The limits are as follows. This is reuse of stored state, not a wider attention window: one block is loaded at a time, and how well a question is answered depends on the model. Writing the memory is a one-time cost, and the store takes terabytes of local NVMe disk. We describe the test protocol, which is built to resist common ways of gaming long-context benchmarks, and give a single-GPU reproduction that uses public software and a free licence for the package.
candidates.reason: vLLMのKV状態を約16K token block単位で暗号化NVMeへ保存し、再利用時にbit-exactで復元するgalahad-kvを50M tokenの公開テキストで検証する。著者要旨はH100/Gemma4 12B・31Bで100/100のblock復元、再計算比2.8～4.3倍高速、GPU energy8.8～12.3倍削減と報告。ただし50M tokenの一括attention窓を実現する方式ではなく、blockを順次復元する持続KVストアである。推論状態のSSD再利用技術としてaccept。

candidates.title: PeekKV: The First Content Token Already Knows Which Heads Matter
candidates.abstract: The size of the KV cache grows linearly with context length, making it a major memory bottleneck in LLM serving. Motivated by recent progress in identifying the functional roles of attention heads, a growing body of work compresses the KV cache non-uniformly across heads. Existing methods either fix the important heads via offline profiling or select them using attention signals from the prefill stage. In both cases, however, accuracy fluctuates substantially across workloads. While investigating the cause of this instability, we find that the active heads shift between the prefill and decode stages even within a single input. Along the decode path, by contrast, the activehead composition remains stable across content tokens once format tokens are filtered out. Based on this observation, we propose PeekKV. PeekKV observes a single content token immediately after prefill - a one-token peek - to jointly obtain head-group scores and token-importance scores. Guided by these scores, PeekKV allocates KV cache budgets to head groups in proportion to their group scores and retains only the top-scoring tokens within each budget. PeekKV requires no offline profiling or training and thus applies directly to unseen workloads and new models. Across four public benchmarks, PeekKV achieves the highest accuracy in more than half of the per-model comparisons against state-of-the-art methods, and stays closest to the full-cache accuracy on RULER and LongBench. On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, PeekKV retains 95.7% of the full-cache accuracy at a 10% memory budget on RULER with 16K contexts and 95.9% at a 1.5% budget on LongBench.
candidates.reason: KV圧縮の重要attention headがprefillとdecodeで変化する点に着目し、prefill直後の最初の内容tokenだけを観測してhead-groupとtokenの重要度を推定する。head-groupに比例したKV予算を配分し各群内で高重要tokenを保持するため、offline profilingや再学習が不要。著者要旨はLlama3.1-8BのRULER 16Kで10%メモリ予算でもfull-cache精度95.7%、LongBenchの1.5%予算で95.9%保持と報告。長文脈KV圧縮としてaccept。

candidates.title: Reorienting the Vector Axis: Restructuring FlashAttention for Long-Vector Processors
candidates.abstract: A Transformer is built around attention, whose cost grows with the square of the sequence length and dominates the layer on long sequences. FlashAttention made that cost manageable by tiling the attention matrix and updating the softmax as it goes, but almost all work since has targeted GPUs. On long-vector processors one vector register can hold up to 512 single-precision numbers. The savings of a vector instruction are proportional to how much of the register it uses, so the choice of which loop to vectorize is a first-order decision. We port PyTorch's CPU FlashAttention kernel to a RISC-V CPU with 2KB vector registers and find that it reaches 16.2% of peak floating-point throughput. The kernel walks each tile one query row at a time: the product against V is vectorized along the 64-element head dimension, the softmax's per-row maximum and sum are reductions that collapse a full register to a scalar, and the software exponential's polynomial coefficients compete with tile data for vector registers and cause spilling. We propose two techniques. The first transposes the score tile and the running output so that queries lie along the contiguous axis. The algorithm and its values are unchanged. A single parameter, the number of queries in a tile, now sets the vector length of every part of the kernel and can be matched to the machine. Both reductions also disappear. The second moves the polynomial's coefficients into scalar registers, removing the spills and cutting the softmax's vector memory instructions by 78.7%. On silicon the two together cut whole-kernel cycles by 1.84 to 2.08x at a head dimension of 64, raising floating-point utilization from 16.2% to 29.7% of peak. An FPGA of the same design ranks the changes identically and scores them higher, at 2.71x.
candidates.reason: 長ベクトルRISC-V CPUでは従来CPU FlashAttentionのhead次元方向vector化が64要素しか使わず、softmax reductionと係数spillで性能を失う。score tileとrunning outputを転置してquery方向にvector化し、exp多項式係数をscalar registerへ移す。著者要旨は2KB vector registerの実シリコンでkernel cycle1.84～2.08倍短縮、peak利用率16.2→29.7%と報告。GPU以外のattention推論kernel最適化としてaccept。
